text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary failure detected in eu-west-1 during region rollout v2 (region_rollout_v2). Health check flapping and 5xx spike. Auto-escalation to on-call.
deploy-bot: Started rollout: region_rollout_v2 -> eu-west-1 (10% traffic), apac-south-1 (0%), global fallback configured.
maya: seeing 502s from inference-gateway-eu. Rolling windows show 3x error rate vs baseline.
samir: @oncall-sre paging you. Pager: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345 :pager:
oncall-sre: ACK. joining. Quick question — is this a code change or infra?
liz: telemetry shows latency +5x and increased queue length on the eu GPU pool. No full OOMs yet.
jon: I can confirm canary health check failed 6/10 probes. Logs: ```2024-05-22T10:34:02Z gateway ERROR upstream 502 downstream timeout tokenize loop```
maya: correlating with a DNS failover event? resolver logs show some APAC edge IPs responding for eu hostnames intermittently.
samir: that would explain cross-region traffic hitting non-warm pools. Any recent DNS TTL changes?
liz: Not intentionally. But control-plane shows a config push: `edge-dns: reduce-ttl` deployed as part of v2 rollout at 10:33Z.
oncall-sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) Kill feature flag region_rollout_v2 2) Abort rollout + rollback 3) Route eu traffic to blue variant. Which do we want?
maya: Recommend kill-switch on the flag first to stop further traffic shift. Low blast radius.
samir: I can flip the kill-switch. Command: `./flags set region_rollout_v2 false --env prod`
jon: before flip, notify customers? There's a small set of higher-SLA customers on eu.
customer-ops: FYI: Customer A (eu) reported degraded responses at 10:36Z via support. Triage team called them and acknowledged potential regression.
oncall-sre: executing kill-switch now. `./flags set region_rollout_v2 false` -> ✅.
incident-bot: ACTION: feature flag region_rollout_v2 set to false by samir at 10:37:12Z. Traffic shift halted.
liz: after flag flip, immediate drop in requests routed to the canary. Error rate trending down. Graphs: errors from 4.8% -> 0.6% in 2 minutes.
maya: good. Next step: roll back the control-plane DNS TTL change and pin edge DNS to previous stable config.
samir: rolling back dns config: `kubectl apply -f edge-dns-stable.yaml` -> submitted.
jon: also starting controlled rollback of the canary image to previous tag: `flux rollback --resource=ksvc/inference-gateway --to-revision=rev-20240518`
oncall-sre: handing off to oncall-sre-night at 10:42Z for monitoring and customer comms. @oncall-night please monitor SLOs for 30m.
oncall-night: ACK. I'll watch latency/error windows and escalate if error budget > 1% sustained.
customer-ops: Notifying affected customers: short status update to Customer A and Customer C, telling them we detected a canary-induced routing issue and flipped the flag; will follow up with RCA.
maya: quick postmortem notes: probable root cause chain: (1) dns-ttl change reduced caching, (2) small rollout caused rapid cross-region probe surface, (3) apac pool cold-warm mismatch caused timeouts -> 502s. Need better pre-checks for dns TTL changes during region rollouts.
jon: action items: 1) add preflight check to block dns-ttl changes if a region rollout is active, 2) add canary probe that validates edge-region IP affinity, 3) add automated rollback if 5xx > 1% within 5m.
samir: I've opened INC-1745 for tracking and will schedule a follow-up war-room at 13:00Z.
incident-bot: Pager cleared for this incident at 10:48Z. Monitoring will continue.
oncall-night: monitoring 30m complete. No customer-visible regressions after 20m. Marking incident as mitigated.
maya: thanks all. Will draft the incident summary and hypothesis for RCA doc. :white_check_mark:
